name: Metre Convention and international metrology
description: An intergovernmental treaty created a permanent institutional framework for cooperation on measurement standards and established the International Bureau of Weights and Measures.

impact.note: A standing international body for an existing metric system; it made measures uniform across many states, and the SI and later unit definitions grew from it.

date.label: 20 May 1875
date.basis: The cited historical account supports 20 May 1875; this is a dated documented episode, not proof of global priority.

events.statement: Representatives of seventeen nations signed the Metre Convention in Paris.

evidence.supports: Date and place of signing, seventeen nations, BIPM and cooperation on units.

evidence.locator: Convention Arts. 1 and 3 and Annexed Regulations Art. 7
evidence.supports: The Convention creates the BIPM and the institutional mandate for the CGPM.

contributions.resource: Signed the convention establishing the framework for international metrology.

evidence.supports: Representatives of seventeen nations signed in Paris and established a permanent structure for coordination.

date.label: 26 September 1889
date.basis: The proceedings date the session and record the votes and allocations.

events.statement: The first CGPM sanctioned the international metre and kilogram prototypes and the calibrated national copies. The recorded allocation by lot assigned kilogram prototypes 4 and 20 to the United States.
events.scope: Sanction and allocation under the Metre Convention. Physical shipment and national use followed separate steps.

evidence.locator: 26 September session, pp. 34–40, especially sanction pp. 38–39 and allocation table p. 40
evidence.supports: Records the sanction, certification process and U.S. allocation.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest episode established by the evidence collected here for this scoped achievement, not a claim of absolute priority.

caveats: The treaty established institutions, not universal adoption of metric units in 1875.

research.note: Independent check of cited event and numerical evidence; wider facets remain sourced, not blanket reviewed. Event contributions, concept, places and extended measure scope were added in a later pass and have not been independently reviewed.
